An incisional biopsy was advised from the buccal mucosa of the left side under local anesthesia after routine blood investigations, which were within normal limits. HIV Tridot screening test was negative. The goal is to diagnose the nature of the lesion based on histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation.

Histopathological examination of the incisional biopsy specimen from the buccal mucosa was performed using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining and evaluated under light microscopy at magnifications of ×100 and ×400. Higher magnification (×400) H&E staining was used to assess nuclear and cytoplasmic details. Additionally, H&E-stained tissue sections at ×400 magnification were examined with focus on tissue architecture and adjacent structures.

At ×100 magnification, a diffuse, monotonous proliferation of round cells arranged in sheets was observed within a loose fibrillar connective tissue stroma; the cells had large nuclei with scant cytoplasm, prominent peripheral nucleoli, chromatin condensation and vesiculation, and nuclear pleomorphism. At ×400 magnification, the cells were round to oval with large nuclei, prominent nucleoli, coarse and vesicular chromatin, occasional nuclear membrane irregularities, and scant faintly eosinophilic cytoplasm; no necrosis or significant inflammation was seen. In the same magnification, infiltration of atypical round cells into adjacent minor salivary gland tissue was noted, with disruption of normal mucous acini architecture; occasional mitotic figures were present.

What can be concluded from these findings regarding the nature of the lesion?

input_logic_chain.research_context: An incisional biopsy was advised from the buccal mucosa of the left side under local anesthesia after routine blood investigations, which were within normal limits. HIV Tridot screening test was negative. The goal is to diagnose the nature of the lesion based on histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation.

experiments.experimental_setting: Histopathological examination of the incisional biopsy specimen from the buccal mucosa using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, evaluated under light microscopy at magnifications of ×100 and ×400.
experiments.experiment_goal: To assess the cellular morphology, architectural pattern, and tissue infiltration of the lesion.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Diffuse, monotonous proliferation of round cells arranged in sheets within a loose fibrillar connective tissue stroma; cells have large nuclei with scant cytoplasm, prominent peripheral nucleoli, chromatin condensation and vesiculation, and nuclear pleomorphism [Image 1].
experiments.interpretation: The diffuse sheet-like growth pattern and monotonous appearance suggest a neoplastic rather than reactive process. The high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, nuclear atypia, and pleomorphism are features of malignant lymphoid proliferation.
experiments.sub_conclusion: The lesion exhibits cytological and architectural features consistent with a malignant lymphoproliferative process.

experiments.experimental_setting: Higher magnification (×400) H&E staining of the same biopsy specimen to evaluate nuclear and cytoplasmic details.
experiments.experiment_goal: To identify specific cytological features such as nucleolar prominence, chromatin pattern, and mitotic activity.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Round to oval cells with large nuclei, prominent nucleoli, coarse and vesicular chromatin, occasional nuclear membrane irregularities, scant faintly eosinophilic cytoplasm, and absence of necrosis or significant inflammation [Image 2].
experiments.interpretation: The presence of prominent nucleoli and vesicular chromatin with focal condensation is characteristic of activated B-cell lymphoblasts or immunoblasts. The lack of necrosis reduces likelihood of highly aggressive tumors like Burkitt lymphoma, but mitotic figures (implied by proliferation) suggest high proliferative activity.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Cytological features are consistent with immunoblastic or centroblastic differentiation, suggestive of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) or similar high-grade lymphoma.

experiments.experimental_setting: H&E-stained tissue section at ×400 magnification with focus on tissue architecture and adjacent structures.
experiments.experiment_goal: To determine whether the atypical cells infiltrate surrounding normal tissue, particularly minor salivary glands.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Infiltration of atypical round cells into adjacent minor salivary gland tissue with disruption of normal mucous acini architecture; occasional mitotic figures are present; no necrosis or prominent inflammation [Image 3].
experiments.interpretation: Infiltration and architectural destruction of native tissue confirm the invasive nature of the proliferation, supporting malignancy. Preservation of some stromal framework without extensive necrosis aligns with DLBCL rather than small non-cleaved cell lymphoma.
experiments.sub_conclusion: The lesion is invasive and destructive, confirming malignancy with lymphoid phenotype.

intermediate_inferences.sub_conclusion: The lesion shows a diffuse, monotonous proliferation of atypical round cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and nuclear pleomorphism.
The cells exhibit cytological features of immunoblasts and centroblasts, including prominent nucleoli and vesicular chromatin.
There is clear infiltration and disruption of minor salivary gland tissue, confirming tissue invasiveness.

reasoning.content: The histopathological analysis reveals a diffuse proliferation of large round cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, nuclear pleomorphism, prominent nucleoli, and vesicular chromatin—features characteristic of aggressive B-cell lymphomas. The monotonous sheet-like growth in a loose stromal background without follicular structures rules out follicular lymphoma. The presence of both centroblast-like [Context] and immunoblast-like cells [Context] aligns with the morphological spectrum of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Infiltration into salivary gland tissue confirms local invasiveness, and the absence of necrosis or starry-sky pattern makes Burkitt lymphoma less likely. The overall pattern does not suggest a low-grade lymphoma due to marked atypia and mitotic activity. While definitive classification requires immunohistochemistry, the histomorphology strongly supports a diagnosis of a high-grade atypical lymphoproliferative lesion, most likely DLBCL.
reasoning.conclusion: The histopathological features are diagnostic of an atypical lymphoproliferative lesion with morphological characteristics highly suggestive of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), pending immunohistochemical confirmation.

question:
A 42-year-old male with a recent history of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) administration for peripheral blood stem cell donation presents with acute kidney injury, tea-colored urine, and urinalysis showing hematuria and mild proteinuria. Renal biopsy was performed to evaluate the underlying cause of kidney injury, with findings suggestive of glomerulonephritis. 

Light microscopy of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded kidney sections stained with hematoxylin and eosin was performed, with a scale bar of 20 μm provided. Additional high-magnification light microscopy of H&E-stained sections focused on glomerular architecture. A separate assessment of tubular and interstitial pathology was also conducted using H&E staining. 

Immunofluorescence microscopy was performed on frozen renal tissue sections using fluorophore-labeled antibodies against IgG, IgM, IgA, C3, C1q, and kappa and lambda light chains, and no fluorescence signal was detected in 2–3 glomeruli examined, including one with a crescent. 

Transmission electron microscopy was performed on glutaraldehyde-fixed, resin-embedded tissue, and no electron-dense deposits were identified in the glomerular basement membranes or mesangium; podocyte foot processes were well-formed, and no fibrils, tubuloreticular inclusions, or amyloid fibrils were observed. 

Serological testing revealed a p-ANCA titer of 1:160 by immunofluorescence, MPO-ANCA level of 74 AU/mL, negative PR3-ANCA and anti-GBM antibodies, ANA titer of 1:160 with negative dsDNA, and normal C3 and C4 levels. 

What is the most likely diagnosis, and how do the histological, immunological, and serological findings collectively support this diagnosis?

input_logic_chain.research_context: Evaluation of the underlying cause of acute kidney injury following G-CSF administration and stem cell donation, with clinical and laboratory features suggestive of glomerulonephritis.

experiments.experimental_setting: Light microscopy of renal biopsy tissue using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, performed on formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded sections of kidney tissue obtained via percutaneous biopsy.
experiments.experiment_goal: To assess structural changes in glomeruli, tubules, interstitium, and vasculature in the context of acute kidney injury.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Segmental necrotizing lesion within the glomerulus with crescent formation along Bowman’s capsule, composed of cells with visible nuclei and cytoplasmic borders; adjacent glomerular tuft shows collapse and eosinophilic debris with nuclear fragmentation; arteriole shows mural thickening, inflammatory infiltration, karyorrhexis, and luminal narrowing; interstitium contains dense inflammatory infiltrate [Image 1].
experiments.interpretation: The crescent formation indicates proliferation of parietal epithelial cells and infiltration of inflammatory cells, characteristic of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. Segmental necrosis with karyorrhexis and inflammatory changes in arterioles suggests active immune-mediated injury. Interstitial inflammation supports ongoing renal inflammation.
experiments.sub_conclusion: There is histological evidence of active, focal necrotizing glomerulonephritis with crescent formation and vascular inflammation.

experiments.experimental_setting: High-magnification light microscopy of H&E-stained renal biopsy sections focusing on glomerular architecture.
experiments.experiment_goal: To evaluate the extent of glomerular structural damage, presence of crescents, and capillary loop integrity.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Segmental area of rarefaction with reduced cellular density; small fibroepithelial crescent adherent to Bowman’s capsule; remaining glomerular tufts show normocellularity with patent capillary lumina; no immune deposits or inflammatory cell accumulation in loops [Image 2].
experiments.interpretation: Segmental rarefaction and crescent formation confirm focal glomerular injury. Normocellularity and open capillary lumina in non-lesional areas suggest the process is not diffuse and lacks hypercellular endocapillary proliferation typically seen in immune-complex glomerulonephritis.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Glomerular injury is focal and segmental, with crescent formation but absence of endocapillary hypercellularity, favoring pauci-immune pathogenesis.

experiments.experimental_setting: Light microscopy of H&E-stained renal biopsy sections assessing tubular and interstitial pathology.
experiments.experiment_goal: To identify tubular injury and interstitial changes contributing to renal dysfunction.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Tubular epithelial cells show cytoplasmic swelling, disrupted architecture, enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and a mitotic figure [arrow]; red cell casts present in tubular lumen with biconcave RBCs embedded in eosinophilic matrix; mild interstitial edema with scattered inflammatory cells [Image 3].
experiments.interpretation: Cytoplasmic swelling and mitotic activity indicate acute tubular injury and regenerative response. Red cell casts are diagnostic of glomerular bleeding, confirming glomerulonephritis. Interstitial inflammation supports active renal disease.
experiments.sub_conclusion: There is acute tubular injury with red cell casts, confirming glomerular origin of hematuria and active renal damage.

experiments.experimental_setting: Immunofluorescence microscopy on frozen renal tissue sections using fluorophore-labeled antibodies against immunoglobulins (IgG, IgM, IgA), complement components (C3, C1q), and light chains (kappa and lambda).
experiments.experiment_goal: To determine the presence of immune complex deposition in glomeruli.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: No fluorescence signal detected for IgG, IgM, IgA, C3, C1q, or light chains in 2–3 glomeruli examined, including one with a crescent [Context].
experiments.interpretation: Absence of immunoglobulin or complement deposition indicates lack of immune complex formation, ruling out immune-complex-mediated glomerulonephritis (e.g., lupus nephritis, post-infectious GN).
experiments.sub_conclusion: Glomerulonephritis is pauci-immune, with no evidence of immune complex deposition.

experiments.experimental_setting: Electron microscopy of glutaraldehyde-fixed, resin-embedded renal biopsy tissue using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to assess ultrastructural features.
experiments.experiment_goal: To detect electron-dense immune deposits, podocyte injury, basement membrane abnormalities, or non-immune deposits.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: No electron-dense deposits in glomerular basement membranes or mesangium; podocyte foot processes are well-formed; no fibrils, tubuloreticular inclusions, or amyloid fibrils [Context].
experiments.interpretation: Absence of electron-dense deposits further confirms lack of immune complex deposition. Intact foot processes suggest minimal podocyte injury. No features of amyloidosis, viral infection, or other systemic diseases.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Ultrastructural analysis supports pauci-immune glomerulonephritis without immune-type deposits or alternative pathologies.

experiments.experimental_setting: Serological testing for autoantibodies including ANA, dsDNA, ANCA (by immunofluorescence), and antigen-specific MPO and PR3 antibodies using ELISA or chemiluminescence assays.
experiments.experiment_goal: To identify serological markers of autoimmune glomerulonephritis, particularly ANCA-associated vasculitis.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Positive p-ANCA by immunofluorescence (titer 1:160); positive MPO-ANCA (74 AU/mL); negative PR3-ANCA and anti-GBM antibodies; positive ANA (1:160) but negative dsDNA; normal C3 and C4 [Context].
experiments.interpretation: p-ANCA with positive MPO-ANCA is highly specific for ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV), particularly microscopic polyangiitis. Negative anti-GBM excludes Goodpasture’s. Positive ANA without dsDNA may be secondary or non-specific.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Serology is consistent with MPO-ANCA-positive vasculitis, supporting pauci-immune necrotizing glomerulonephritis.

intermediate_inferences.sub_conclusion: There is histological evidence of active, focal necrotizing glomerulonephritis with crescent formation and vascular inflammation.
Glomerular injury is focal and segmental, with crescent formation but absence of endocapillary hypercellularity, favoring pauci-immune pathogenesis.
There is acute tubular injury with red cell casts, confirming glomerular origin of hematuria and active renal damage.
Glomerulonephritis is pauci-immune, with no evidence of immune complex deposition.
Serology is consistent with MPO-ANCA-positive vasculitis, supporting pauci-immune necrotizing glomerulonephritis.

reasoning.content: The renal biopsy demonstrates focal segmental necrotizing glomerulonephritis with crescent formation, as seen in [Image 1] and [Image 2], confirming active glomerular inflammation. The absence of endocapillary hypercellularity and immune deposits on immunofluorescence and electron microscopy rules out immune-complex-mediated diseases. Instead, the findings are characteristic of pauci-immune glomerulonephritis. The presence of red cell casts in tubules ([Image 3]) confirms glomerular hemorrhage, and acute tubular injury reflects downstream damage. Critically, serological detection of MPO-ANCA with p-ANCA pattern provides strong evidence for ANCA-associated vasculitis, specifically microscopic polyangiitis. While ANA is positive, the absence of dsDNA and normal complement levels makes lupus nephritis unlikely. The temporal association with G-CSF use—a known trigger of ANCA activation and vasculitis—suggests a probable drug-induced exacerbation or unmasking of underlying autoimmune susceptibility. Together, histopathological, immunological, and serological data converge on a diagnosis of MPO-ANCA-associated pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis.
reasoning.conclusion: The patient developed MPO-ANCA-positive pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis, likely triggered or unmasked by G-CSF administration, leading to acute kidney injury following stem cell donation.

question:
A 46-year-old fisherman presents with a chronic, raised, red-purple, verrucous lesion on the right knee and erythematous crusted plaques on the left foot, with clinical and histopathological features suggestive of cutaneous tuberculosis, particularly tuberculosis verrucosa cutis (TVC). To investigate the etiology, the following studies were performed:

- A skin biopsy was processed with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining and examined under light microscopy at 4x and 40x magnification.
- Periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) staining was performed on the skin biopsy tissue.
- Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) staining was performed on pus and skin scrapings.
- Skin scraping was examined with 10% potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparation under light microscopy.
- Tissue culture was performed using Sabouraud dextrose agar.
- A chest radiograph was performed using standard posterior-anterior projection.
- The Mantoux tuberculin skin test was administered with intradermal purified protein derivative (PPD), and induration was measured after 48–72 hours.
- Mycobacterial culture was performed using skin tissue inoculated onto appropriate media and incubated for up to four weeks.
- GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay was performed on the tissue sample using real-time PCR.
- Interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) was performed using ELISA on peripheral blood.
- Empirical anti-tuberculosis treatment (ATT) with a category 1 regimen was initiated, and the patient was monitored clinically over 6 months.

The following findings were observed:
- PAS staining did not reveal any fungal structures.
- ZN staining did not show acid-fast bacilli.
- KOH preparation did not show hyphae, spores, or muriform bodies.
- No fungal growth was observed on Sabouraud dextrose agar.
- The chest radiograph showed no parenchymal infiltrates, cavitations, or lymphadenopathy.
- The Mantoux test showed 9 mm of induration.
- Mycobacterial culture did not yield growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
- GeneXpert did not detect M. tuberculosis DNA in the tissue.
- IGRA was positive.
- After 21 days of ATT, thinning of the plaque and reduced pruritus were observed; by 6 months, there was significant clinical improvement with resolution of crusting and flattening of the lesions.

What is the most likely diagnosis, and how is it supported by the clinical, histopathological, laboratory, and therapeutic findings in this case?

input_logic_chain.research_context: To determine the underlying etiology of a chronic, raised, red-purple, verrucous lesion on the right knee and erythematous crusted plaques on the left foot in a 46-year-old fisherman, with clinical and histopathological features suggestive of cutaneous tuberculosis, particularly tuberculosis verrucosa cutis (TVC).

experiments.experimental_setting: Skin biopsy was performed and tissue sections were stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) for histopathological evaluation. The slides were examined under light microscopy at low (4x) and high (40x) magnification.
experiments.experiment_goal: To assess the epidermal and dermal architectural changes and characterize the inflammatory infiltrate in the skin lesion.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: At 4x magnification: The epidermis shows irregular thickening with downward projections and a wavy, undulating base. The stratum corneum is prominent. The dermis shows disrupted collagen architecture with pale, interspersed areas and increased cellularity [Image 1]. At 40x magnification: Dermal tissue reveals a dense infiltrate of small, darkly stained round cells and larger cells with multi-lobed nuclei, diffusely distributed without compartmentalization. The stroma appears eosinophilic and fibrillar [Image 2].
experiments.interpretation: The irregular thickening of the epidermis with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia suggests a reactive or chronic inflammatory process. The dense, mixed inflammatory infiltrate composed of lymphocytes (small hyperchromatic nuclei) and neutrophils (multi-lobed nuclei) extending from superficial to deep dermis indicates a chronic suppurative inflammation. The absence of granulomatous architecture or caseation does not exclude mycobacterial infection, as TVC may lack classic granulomas.
experiments.sub_conclusion: The histopathological findings are consistent with chronic suppurative inflammation, which may occur in deep fungal infections or cutaneous tuberculosis, including TVC [Image 1, Image 2].

experiments.experimental_setting: Periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) staining was performed on the skin biopsy tissue to detect fungal organisms.
experiments.experiment_goal: To identify the presence of fungal elements such as hyphae, spores, or yeast forms in the tissue.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: No fungal structures (e.g., septate hyphae, budding yeast, or muriform cells) were observed in the tissue sections [Context].
experiments.interpretation: PAS staining highlights polysaccharide components in fungal cell walls. The absence of positively stained structures indicates no detectable fungal organisms in the sampled tissue.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Fungal infection, including chromoblastomycosis, is unlikely [Context].

experiments.experimental_setting: Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) staining was performed on pus and skin scrapings to detect acid-fast bacilli (AFB).
experiments.experiment_goal: To identify Mycobacterium tuberculosis or other mycobacterial species in exudative material.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: No acid-fast bacilli (red, rod-shaped organisms) were observed in the stained smears [Context].
experiments.interpretation: AFB are characteristic of mycobacterial infections. Their absence in ZN staining reduces the likelihood of active mycobacterial discharge but does not rule out paucibacillary disease such as TVC, where organisms are often scarce.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Absence of AFB does not exclude cutaneous tuberculosis, especially in paucibacillary forms like TVC [Context].

experiments.experimental_setting: Skin scraping was examined with 10% potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparation under light microscopy.
experiments.experiment_goal: To detect fungal hyphae or spores in the superficial layers of the lesion.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: No hyphae, spores, or muriform bodies were observed [Context].
experiments.interpretation: KOH dissolves keratin, allowing visualization of fungal elements. The absence of such structures suggests no superficial fungal infection.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Superficial fungal etiology, such as dermatophytosis or chromoblastomycosis, is unlikely [Context].

experiments.experimental_setting: Tissue culture was performed using Sabouraud dextrose agar under appropriate incubation conditions to isolate fungal pathogens.
experiments.experiment_goal: To grow and identify potential fungal organisms from the skin lesion.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: No visible fungal growth was observed on Sabouraud agar after incubation [Context].
experiments.interpretation: Lack of growth suggests absence of cultivable fungi in the tissue sample.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Deep fungal infection, including chromoblastomycosis or other mycoses, is not supported by culture evidence [Context].

experiments.experimental_setting: Chest radiograph was performed using standard posterior-anterior projection.
experiments.experiment_goal: To evaluate for evidence of pulmonary tuberculosis, which may accompany cutaneous TB.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: No parenchymal infiltrates, cavitations, or lymphadenopathy were observed in the chest radiograph [Figure 2A].
experiments.interpretation: Absence of radiographic abnormalities suggests no active pulmonary tuberculosis.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Pulmonary involvement is not present, supporting isolated cutaneous disease [Context].

experiments.experimental_setting: Mantoux tuberculin skin test was administered with intradermal injection of purified protein derivative (PPD), and induration measured after 48–72 hours.
experiments.experiment_goal: To assess cell-mediated immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Induration measured 9 mm, interpreted as negative according to standard criteria [Figure 2B].
experiments.interpretation: A negative Mantoux test may occur in paucibacillary disease, localized infection, or immune modulation, and does not rule out TB, especially in cutaneous forms.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Negative Mantoux test does not exclude cutaneous tuberculosis [Context].

experiments.experimental_setting: Mycobacterial culture was performed using skin tissue sample inoculated onto appropriate media (e.g., Lowenstein-Jensen) and incubated for up to four weeks.
experiments.experiment_goal: To isolate and identify Mycobacterium tuberculosis from the lesion.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: No growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis was observed after four weeks of culture [Context].
experiments.interpretation: Culture is highly specific but has low sensitivity in paucibacillary conditions like TVC due to low organism load.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Negative culture does not rule out cutaneous tuberculosis [Context].

experiments.experimental_setting: GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay was performed on tissue sample using real-time PCR to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA and rifampicin resistance.
experiments.experiment_goal: To molecularly detect M. tuberculosis DNA in the tissue with high sensitivity and specificity.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: GeneXpert test did not detect M. tuberculosis DNA in the tissue sample [Context].
experiments.interpretation: False-negative results may occur in paucibacillary disease due to low bacterial load or poor sample quality.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Absence of M. tuberculosis DNA by GeneXpert does not definitively exclude TVC [Context].

experiments.experimental_setting: Interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) was performed using ELISA method on peripheral blood to detect T-cell response to M. tuberculosis-specific antigens (e.g., ESAT-6, CFP-10).
experiments.experiment_goal: To assess systemic immune sensitization to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: IGRA result was positive, indicating release of interferon-gamma in response to TB-specific antigens [Context].
experiments.interpretation: A positive IGRA indicates prior or current infection with M. tuberculosis, even in the absence of active pulmonary disease.
experiments.sub_conclusion: The patient has immunological evidence of M. tuberculosis infection, supporting a diagnosis of cutaneous tuberculosis [Context].

experiments.experimental_setting: Empirical anti-tuberculosis treatment (ATT) was initiated with category 1 regimen: 4 drugs (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) for 2 months, followed by 2 drugs (rifampicin, isoniazid) for 4 months. Clinical response was monitored over 6 months.
experiments.experiment_goal: To assess clinical response to ATT as a diagnostic and therapeutic trial for suspected TVC.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: After 21 days: Thinning of the plaque and reduced pruritus. At 6 months: Significant clinical improvement with resolution of crusting and flattening of lesions [Figure 4].
experiments.interpretation: Rapid and sustained improvement on ATT is highly suggestive of a mycobacterial etiology, particularly in cases with supportive clinical and immunological findings.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Therapeutic response supports the diagnosis of tuberculosis verrucosa cutis [Context].

intermediate_inferences.sub_conclusion: Histopathology reveals chronic suppurative inflammation with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and mixed lymphocytic-neutrophilic infiltrate, consistent with deep infection such as cutaneous TB or deep mycosis.
Fungal etiologies (chromoblastomycosis, dermatophytosis) are excluded by negative KOH, PAS, culture, and Sabouraud results.
Cutaneous tuberculosis remains plausible despite negative ZN, Mantoux, culture, and GeneXpert, due to the paucibacillary nature of TVC.
Positive IGRA confirms systemic immune sensitization to M. tuberculosis, supporting TB infection.
Marked clinical improvement on ATT provides strong diagnostic validation for TVC.

reasoning.content: The patient presented with chronic, crusted, verrucous skin lesions clinically suggestive of tuberculosis verrucosa cutis. Histopathology demonstrated pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and dense mixed dermal inflammation, indicative of chronic suppurative process. Although fungal infections were considered in the differential, they were systematically excluded by negative KOH, PAS, and culture. Cutaneous TB remained the leading diagnosis despite negative direct detection methods (ZN, GeneXpert, culture) and negative Mantoux, which are known to have low sensitivity in paucibacillary disease. The positive IGRA provided immunological evidence of M. tuberculosis exposure. Most critically, the patient showed rapid and sustained clinical improvement on anti-tuberculosis therapy, which served as a diagnostic-therapeutic confirmation. Together, the clinical picture, histopathological findings, exclusion of mimics, positive IGRA, and therapeutic response form a coherent diagnostic chain.
reasoning.conclusion: The patient is diagnosed with tuberculosis verrucosa cutis based on clinical presentation, histopathological findings of chronic suppurative inflammation, exclusion of fungal and other mimicking conditions, positive IGRA, and excellent response to anti-tuberculosis therapy despite negative direct microbiological tests.

question: In the histologic assessment of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) in breast cancer, H&E-stained tissue sections are examined under light microscopy at high-power magnification to evaluate the stromal area within the tumor border. Two representative cases were analyzed: in one, mononuclear inflammatory cells were densely present in the stroma; in the other, such cells were sparsely and unevenly distributed among tumor cell clusters and stromal regions. Based on these findings, what can be concluded about the feasibility and biological significance of assessing TILs using H&E-stained sections in breast cancer?

input_logic_chain.research_context: Histologic assessment of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) in breast cancer using H&E-stained tissue sections under light microscopy at high magnification, reported as the percentage area occupied by mononuclear inflammatory cells in the stromal area within the tumor border.

experiments.experimental_setting: H&E-stained breast cancer tissue sections were examined under light microscopy with high-power magnification to assess the stromal area infiltrated by mononuclear inflammatory cells (lymphocytes and plasma cells).
experiments.experiment_goal: To evaluate the density and distribution of TILs within the intratumoral stroma for prognostic assessment.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: In Image 1, there is a dense infiltration of small, round lymphocytes with darkly stained, hyperchromatic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, diffusely distributed and forming aggregates within the fibrous stroma [Image 1]. In Image 2, lymphocytes are sparsely scattered, with low density and uneven distribution among tumor cell clusters and stroma [Image 2].
experiments.interpretation: The presence and density of lymphocytes in the stromal compartment reflect the host immune response against the tumor. Dense lymphocytic infiltration (as in Image 1) indicates a robust immune reaction, while sparse infiltration (as in Image 2) suggests a weaker response.
experiments.sub_conclusion: TIL density can be visually assessed on H&E slides and varies significantly between tumors, with some showing intense stromal infiltration and others minimal presence.

intermediate_inferences.sub_conclusion: TIL density is assessable via H&E staining and exhibits inter-tumoral heterogeneity in spatial distribution and abundance.

reasoning.content: The experimental observation confirms that TILs can be identified and semi-quantitatively assessed using standard H&E staining. The visual distinction between high (Image 1) and low (Image 2) TIL infiltration supports the feasibility of histologic scoring. Although H&E does not allow lineage-specific identification, the morphologic features (small round cells with dark nuclei) are consistent with mononuclear inflammatory cells such as lymphocytes. This morphologic assessment forms the basis for TIL scoring in routine pathology, which has been validated in multiple studies as a prognostic biomarker.
reasoning.conclusion: Histologic assessment of TILs on H&E-stained sections is a feasible and reproducible method to evaluate the immune component of the breast cancer tumor microenvironment, with high TIL levels indicating a stronger anti-tumor immune response.

question: In the 2017 WHO classification, minimally invasive follicular thyroid carcinoma (FTC) is classified as either minimally invasive (capsular invasion only) or encapsulated angioinvasive (with or without capsular invasion), and the extent of vascular invasion is prognostically relevant. A study was conducted involving histological examination of thyroid nodules using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. One examination focused on capsular integrity in a follicular-patterned tumor. Another examination focused on vascular invasion patterns within a vascular channel of an encapsulated follicular tumor. Based on these experiments, what can be concluded regarding the classification of the two tumors according to the 2017 WHO criteria?

input_logic_chain.research_context: In the 2017 WHO classification, minimally invasive follicular thyroid carcinoma (FTC) is classified as either minimally invasive (capsular invasion only) or encapsulated angioinvasive (with or without capsular invasion), and the extent of vascular invasion is prognostically relevant.

experiments.experimental_setting: Histological examination of a thyroid nodule using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, focusing on capsular integrity and vascular invasion patterns.
experiments.experiment_goal: To assess the presence and extent of capsular invasion in a follicular-patterned thyroid tumor.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: The histological section displays a well-circumscribed nodule surrounded by a fibrous capsule, with partial disruption of the capsule in multiple areas and clusters of cells extending beyond it into the adjacent stroma [Image 1].
experiments.interpretation: Disruption of the fibrous capsule with tumor cell extension into the adjacent stroma indicates capsular invasion, a key diagnostic criterion for malignancy in follicular neoplasms.
experiments.sub_conclusion: The tumor in Image 1 exhibits capsular invasion, fulfilling a criterion for malignant classification under the minimally invasive FTC category.

experiments.experimental_setting: Histological examination of a thyroid nodule using H&E staining, focusing on intravascular tumor cell presence within a vascular channel.
experiments.experiment_goal: To determine whether vascular invasion is present in an encapsulated follicular tumor.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: A vascular channel within the encapsulated lesion contains clusters of neoplastic cells within its lumen, with no visible disruption of the vessel wall [Image 2].
experiments.interpretation: The presence of tumor cell clusters within an endothelial-lined vascular space, without vessel wall rupture, confirms vascular invasion, which is diagnostic of angioinvasion in encapsulated FTC.
experiments.sub_conclusion: The tumor in Image 2 demonstrates vascular invasion, supporting classification as encapsulated angioinvasive FTC.

intermediate_inferences.sub_conclusion: Capsular invasion is present in Image 1, consistent with minimally invasive FTC.
Vascular invasion is present in Image 2, supporting diagnosis of encapsulated angioinvasive FTC.

reasoning.content: Based on the 2017 WHO classification, follicular thyroid carcinomas are subdivided based on invasion patterns. The tumor in Image 1 shows multifocal capsular disruption with tumor extension into the surrounding stroma but no vascular invasion. This pattern satisfies the criteria for minimally invasive FTC (capsular invasion only). In contrast, Image 2 reveals intravascular tumor cell clusters within a vascular channel of an encapsulated tumor, confirming vascular invasion. Since the tumor remains encapsulated and shows no extensive parenchymal invasion, this aligns with the definition of encapsulated angioinvasive FTC. Both tumors lack nuclear features of papillary thyroid carcinoma and exhibit follicular architecture, confirming follicular cell lineage. Therefore, the two images represent distinct subtypes of minimally invasive FTC as defined in the 2017 WHO classification.
reasoning.conclusion: Image 1 represents minimally invasive FTC with capsular invasion only, while Image 2 represents encapsulated angioinvasive FTC, demonstrating that both entities are distinct subtypes under the 2017 WHO classification of FTC based on invasion patterns.

question:
In the context of identifying and characterizing myofibroblasts in low malignant potential (LMP) lesions with emphasis on their smooth muscle cell (SMC) origin and synthetic activity in extracellular matrix (ECM) production, the following investigations were conducted:

- Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis of tissue specimens from LMP lesions was performed using standard fixation, embedding, and ultrathin sectioning techniques.
- TEM imaging of tangentially sectioned cells from LMP lesions was carried out to assess organelle distribution and cell-matrix interface structures.
- High-magnification TEM of LMP lesion cells was used to examine nuclear morphology, cytoplasmic organelles, and cell surface matrix interactions.
- Immunohistochemical (IHC) staining of LMP lesion tissues for Factor VIII-related antigen and smooth muscle actin (SMA) was performed, along with histological staining (H&E and trichrome).
- Ultrastructural analysis of cell-matrix junctions and ECM composition in LMP lesions was conducted via TEM.

It was observed that the LMP lesions were frequently lined by one or more layers of pleomorphic, hyperchromatic, amphophilic cells that were strongly positive for both Factor VIII-related antigen and SMA.

What can be concluded from these investigations regarding the identity, origin, and functional activity of the cells lining LMP lesions?

input_logic_chain.research_context: Identification and characterization of myofibroblasts in LMP (low malignant potential) lesions based on ultrastructural and immunohistochemical features, with emphasis on their smooth muscle cell (SMC) origin and synthetic activity in extracellular matrix (ECM) production.

experiments.experimental_setting: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis of tissue specimens from LMP lesions, using standard fixation, embedding, and ultrathin sectioning techniques to visualize subcellular structures at high resolution.
experiments.experiment_goal: To identify ultrastructural hallmarks of myofibroblastic differentiation in LMP lesion cells.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Abundant and prominently expanded rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER), appearing as extensive, parallel cisternae occupying a significant portion of the intracellular space; sparse actin filaments and dense bodies; sub-plasmalemmal dense plaques; preserved external lamina surrounding the cell [Image 1].
experiments.interpretation: The marked expansion of RER indicates heightened protein synthetic activity, a hallmark of myofibroblasts. The presence of dense plaques and sparse actin-dense body bundles suggests a transitional cytoskeletal architecture between SMCs and myofibroblasts. Preservation of external lamina is indicative of partial retention of SMC lineage features.
experiments.sub_conclusion: The cells in LMP lesions exhibit ultrastructural features consistent with myofibroblastic differentiation while retaining some SMC-derived characteristics.

experiments.experimental_setting: TEM imaging of tangentially sectioned cells from LMP lesions to assess cytoplasmic organelle distribution and cell-matrix interface structures.
experiments.experiment_goal: To evaluate the relative abundance of RER, cytoskeletal elements, and extracellular matrix contacts in myofibroblasts.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Abundant interconnected, stacked RER with ribosomal particles; filamentous actin structures intermingled with RER in roughly comparable abundance; dense bodies present but not dominant; sub-plasmalemmal dense plaques sparsely distributed; extracellular fibrillar deposits corresponding to shed external lamina and fibronectin [Image 2].
experiments.interpretation: The prominence of RER supports active synthetic function. The coexistence of actin filaments and dense bodies, though not organized into thick bundles, indicates residual contractile potential. The presence of shed external lamina and fibronectin in the extracellular space suggests active remodeling and secretion of ECM components.
experiments.sub_conclusion: LMP lesion cells display a synthetic phenotype with ongoing ECM production and partial retention of contractile apparatus, consistent with myofibroblast identity.

experiments.experimental_setting: High-magnification TEM of LMP lesion cells to examine nuclear morphology, cytoplasmic organelles, and cell surface matrix interactions.
experiments.experiment_goal: To assess nuclear atypia, synthetic organelle abundance, and evidence of matrix-producing activity at the plasma membrane.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Large, irregularly shaped nucleus with prominent nucleolus and chromatin depletion; densely packed RER studded with ribosomes, more abundant than peripheral actin and dense bodies; discontinuous external lamina; fibronectin as elongated, electron-dense fibrous strands extending from the cell [Image 3].
experiments.interpretation: Nuclear pleomorphism and prominent nucleoli reflect high transcriptional activity. The predominance of RER over contractile elements further supports a synthetic myofibroblast phenotype. Fibronectin filaments extending from the membrane suggest active deposition into the ECM, forming fibronexus-like structures.
experiments.sub_conclusion: The cells exhibit nuclear and cytoplasmic features of activated myofibroblasts engaged in extracellular matrix synthesis.

experiments.experimental_setting: Immunohistochemical (IHC) staining of LMP lesion tissues for Factor VIII-related antigen and smooth muscle actin (SMA), combined with histological staining (H&E and trichrome).
experiments.experiment_goal: To determine endothelial versus mesenchymal lineage and confirm myofibroblast marker expression.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: LMP lesions lined by pleomorphic, hyperchromatic, amphophilic cells strongly positive for both Factor VIII-related antigen and SMA [Context].
experiments.interpretation: Co-expression of Factor VIII-related antigen (typically endothelial) and SMA (mesenchymal/SMC marker) suggests either aberrant antigen expression or transdifferentiation. However, ultrastructural evidence lacks endothelial features (e.g., Weibel-Palade bodies, fenestrations), supporting a mesenchymal origin with possible antigenic mimicry.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Despite Factor VIII positivity, the ultrastructural profile supports a mesenchymal, not endothelial, origin of these cells.

experiments.experimental_setting: Ultrastructural analysis of cell-matrix junctions and ECM composition in LMP lesions via TEM.
experiments.experiment_goal: To identify fibronexus complexes and characterize ECM components associated with myofibroblasts.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Electron-dense fibronectin filaments extending from plasma membranes and forming fibronexus-like structures; parallel rows of banded collagen fibrils oriented perpendicular to the plasma membrane; elastin with granular and fibrillar morphology; glycosaminoglycan particles [Image 1, Image 2, Image 3].
experiments.interpretation: Fibronexus complexes and perpendicular collagen deposition are hallmark features of active collagen-producing myofibroblasts. The presence of elastin and glycosaminoglycans indicates a complex, dynamically remodeled ECM typical of reactive or neoplastic stromal environments.
experiments.sub_conclusion: The ECM architecture and cell-matrix interactions confirm active matrix synthesis by myofibroblasts in LMP lesions.

intermediate_inferences.sub_conclusion: The cells in LMP lesions display ultrastructural features of myofibroblasts, including expanded RER, sparse stress fibers, and sub-plasmalemmal dense plaques.
These myofibroblasts retain features of SMC origin, including external lamina and pinocytic vesicles, despite phenotypic transition.
The extracellular matrix shows evidence of active deposition, including fibronexus complexes and organized collagen fibrils, confirming functional synthetic activity.
Immunophenotypic data showing Factor VIII and SMA co-expression do not override ultrastructural evidence of mesenchymal origin.

reasoning.content: The integration of TEM findings across multiple images reveals that LMP lesion cells exhibit classic ultrastructural hallmarks of myofibroblasts: prominent RER indicating high synthetic activity, sparse actin-dense body bundles reflecting reduced contractility, and sub-plasmalemmal dense plaques associated with fibronectin filaments—features consistent with fibronexus formation. Despite these changes, the preservation of external lamina and pinocytic vesicles supports their derivation from smooth muscle cells. The absence of gap junctions and presence of mesenchymal junctions further support a myofibroblast phenotype rather than a true SMC or endothelial lineage. Although IHC shows Factor VIII-related antigen positivity, which may suggest endothelial differentiation, the lack of endothelial ultrastructure (e.g., thin cytoplasm, lumens, Weibel-Palade bodies) and the presence of myofibroblast-specific features refute this interpretation. Instead, this likely represents aberrant antigen expression. The ECM composition—organized collagen, fibronectin filaments, elastin, and glycosaminoglycans—reflects active remodeling driven by these cells. Since TEM is the gold standard for myofibroblast identification in the absence of specific IHC markers, these collective observations definitively establish the presence of SMC-derived myofibroblasts in LMP lesions.
reasoning.conclusion: LMP lesions are lined by myofibroblasts derived from smooth muscle cells, as confirmed by ultrastructural evidence of synthetic phenotype, partial retention of SMC features, and active extracellular matrix production, despite ambiguous immunohistochemical staining.

question:
A 28-year-old patient presents with chronic cyanosis but has a normal cardiovascular examination, no murmurs, and normal pulmonary function. To evaluate for underlying structural myocardial abnormalities that may contribute to or coexist with the observed clinical phenotype, endomyocardial biopsies were obtained from both the right and left ventricles via transatrial access through an atrial communication. All histological sections were examined under light microscopy with a scale bar of 100 μm.

- The right ventricular biopsy was processed with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining.
- A second section from the same right ventricular sample was stained with Mason trichrome.
- The left ventricular biopsy was also processed with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining.
- A second section from the left ventricular sample was stained with Mason trichrome.

What can be concluded from these histological findings, and how do they inform the underlying myocardial pathology in this patient?

input_logic_chain.research_context: Evaluation of myocardial tissue pathology in a patient presenting with cyanosis and normal cardiovascular examination, to determine underlying structural myocardial abnormalities that may contribute to or coexist with the observed clinical phenotype.

experiments.experimental_setting: Endomyocardial biopsy samples were obtained from both the right and left ventricles via transatrial access through an atrial communication. Tissue sections were processed for histological analysis using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Mason trichrome staining methods. The samples were examined under light microscopy for architectural and cellular abnormalities.
experiments.experiment_goal: To identify histopathological changes in myocardial tissue, particularly fibrosis, inflammation, necrosis, or structural disarray, that may explain impaired cardiac function or contribute to the clinical presentation.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: In the right ventricular biopsy, H&E staining reveals elongated eosinophilic myocardial fibers with preserved striations in some areas, interspersed with dense, pale pink, acellular, wavy connective tissue predominantly localized in the subendocardial region [Image 1].
experiments.interpretation: The pale pink, acellular, wavy material observed under H&E staining is consistent with collagenous fibrosis. Its subendocardial predominance and disruption of myocardial fiber continuity suggest chronic structural remodeling of the myocardium, likely due to prior injury or hemodynamic stress.
experiments.sub_conclusion: The right ventricular myocardium exhibits subendocardial and intramyocardial fibrosis, indicating chronic myocardial remodeling.

experiments.experimental_setting: Same as above: right ventricular endomyocardial biopsy stained with Mason trichrome, where collagen is stained blue and muscle fibers red/pink.
experiments.experiment_goal: To confirm and better delineate fibrotic deposits using a collagen-specific stain and assess spatial distribution and tissue architecture.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: Blue-stained irregular patches, streaks, and clusters are observed within the myocardium, especially in the subendocardial region, with a gradual transition between fibrotic and non-fibrotic areas and no sharp demarcation [Image 2].
experiments.interpretation: The blue staining confirms the presence of collagen-rich extracellular matrix deposition, characteristic of fibrosis. The gradual transition and lack of sharp boundaries suggest chronic, progressive fibrotic infiltration rather than acute or focal scarring.
experiments.sub_conclusion: Trichrome staining confirms subendocardial and intramyocardial fibrosis in the right ventricle with features of chronic, progressive deposition.

experiments.experimental_setting: Left ventricular endomyocardial biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), examined under light microscopy.
experiments.experiment_goal: To assess whether fibrotic changes are confined to the right ventricle or are biventricular in distribution.
experiments.visual_phenomenon: The left ventricular section shows regular, densely packed eosinophilic myocytes with areas of pale, homogenous, acellular tissue distributed irregularly within the myocardium and concentrated subendocardially.
